merger_description:
Funds or vehicles managed and advised by affiliates of CVC Capital Partners plc (**CVC plc**) (**CVC Funds**, and together with its affiliates and CVC Capital Partners plc and its subsidiaries, **CVC**) proposes to acquire all the issued and outstanding equity interests in, and sole control over, over Chess Holdings, LLC (**Chess Holdings** and collectively with its subsidiaries, the **Target**).

The acquirer is Squares Blocker, Inc. (the **Acquirer**), a newly incorporated corporation under the laws of Delaware. The Acquirer is indirectly controlled by funds or vehicles advised or managed by affiliates of CVC. The CVC Network is a global alternative investment manager focused on private equity, credit, infrastructure and secondaries, and includes CVC plc and each of its subsidiaries from time to time and the CVC Funds. CVC plc is a public limited company whose shares are listed and admitted to trading on the Euronext Amsterdam Stock Exchange. As it relates to the CVC Network’s private equity activities, CVC plc, and certain of its subsidiaries from time to time, provide investment advice to and/or manage investments on behalf of CVC Funds.

The Target, headquartered in the United States, operates under the commercial name ‘Chess.com’ and is a provider of chess gaming and other chess-related services including forum and social network, a news feed, a chess academy, a coaching platform, tactics and puzzles, live tournaments, and a separate website for kids (Chesskid.com), and ChessTV.

As of February 2026, Chess.com had over 248 million registered users, with a presence across more than 200 countries. The Target is an entirely virtual company with no physical presence apart from a small office in Utah and in Spain.

The Target is currently majority-owned by funds managed and advised by General Atlantic, L.P. (**GA**), a global growth equity firm headquartered in New York, with the remainder held by management and other minority investors. Following completion of the Transaction, funds managed and advised by GA will retain a non-controlling minority stake of 14% in the Target through a co-investment alongside the CVC Funds.

determination_table_content.details:
Squares Blocker, Inc., a newly incorporated corporation indirectly
controlled by funds or vehicles advised or managed by affiliates of
CVC Capital Partners plc (CVC Capital Partners) applied for a
notification waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of all issued
and outstanding equity interests in, and sole control of, Chess
Holdings, LLC (trading as Chess.com), as described in the
transaction documents provided as part of the application (the
Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Squares Blocker, Inc. is indirectly controlled by funds
advised or managed by affiliates of CVC Capital Partners, a public
limited company incorporated in Jersey and listed in Amsterdam.
The CVC Network is a global alternative investment manager
focused on private equity, credit, infrastructure, and secondaries.
The target, Chess.com, is headquartered in the United States and is a
provider of chess gaming and other chess-related services including
a forum and social network, a news feed, a chess academy, a
coaching platform, tactics and puzzles, live tournaments, a separate
website for kids (Chesskid.com), and ChessTV. As of February 2026,
Chess.com had over 248 million registered users, with a presence
across more than 200 countries.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between CVC Capital Partners
and Chess.com in the supply of online chess or chess-
related services
b. the parties’ combined share in the supply of online video
games to customers in Australia is low
c. the presence of alternative suppliers of online video games
in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
